::: {#exm-map-normal-normal}
#### The MAP estimate of a Gaussian mean

In @exm-normal-normal,
the posterior is $\ndist{\frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x}, \frac{1}{n+1}}$.
A Gaussian density is largest at its mean,
so

$$\hth_{\text{MAP}} = \frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x}.$$

@cor-map-penalized gives the same answer from the penalized form.
Up to terms that do not involve $\mu$,
the negative log-likelihood is $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2$
and the penalty is $\frac{1}{2}\mu^2$.
Setting the derivative of their sum to zero gives

$$
\ba
0
&= -\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu) + \mu
&& \text{(derivative of the sum with respect to $\mu$)}\\
&= -n\bar{x} + n\mu + \mu
&& \text{($\sum_i x_i = n\bar{x}$)}\\
&= (n+1)\mu - n\bar{x},
&& \text{(collecting the terms in $\mu$)}
\ea
$$

so $\mu = \frac{n}{n+1}\bar{x}$.
The penalty $\frac{1}{2}\mu^2$ pulls the estimate toward the prior mean $0$,
and its pull weakens relative to the data as $n$ grows.
:::
